scope_finding: The274-case suite establishes extra1-clock sensitivity only. Exact saved80MHz/iomux-false SDK path implies extra_dummy2; full runtime/QIO problem remains unproven by this correction and must stay NONPASS until observed.
reasoning: SSI sends complete bytes, and the old ceil(total bits) promotes every residual1..7bits into a whole additional byte, consuming real response data. The proposed complete-byte floor plus clamp is a coherent conservative quantization inside this existing functional model.

The applied conditional form is algebraically MAX(floor((addr_bits+clocks*lanes)/8),ceil(addr_bits/8))-ceil(addr_bits/8). It counts complete combined bytes and cannot subtract below the already emitted address bytes. It avoids unsigned underflow and remains identical to the old formula whenever combined phase bits are divisible by8.

Whole-byte baselines remain: QIO28/5 gives4address+2dummy bytes, DIO28/2 gives4+0, QIO24/6 gives3+3, DIO24/4 gives3+1, fast/DOUT/QOUT24/8 gives3+1. With one extra compensation clock these totals remain unchanged; JEDEC addr0/dummy1 produces no whole dummy byte.

This does not accurately emulate real fractional wire bits or analog MISO latency. Physical devices still see compensation clocks; the functional model discards only the unrepresentable fractional-byte remainder, without returning fabricated IDs, changing backing data or disabling a firmware assertion.

A general accurate solution would model bit-level SPI and the receiver sampling delay explicitly. Do not silently drop arbitrary full-byte dummy excess or clamp to opcode-specific expected minima: that would hide configured timing/protocol behavior.
SDK_primary_chain: esp_flash_spi_init.c:116-123 ESP32 default iomux=false/input_delay_ns0 and selected DEFAULT_FLASH_SPEED; :526 assigns source frequency.

spi_flash_hal.c:63-79 computes compensation from input/GPIO delay; :125 binds extra_dummy. common.inc:24,163-165 adds extra_dummy to protocol dummy length, and :213-215 avoids input compensation on transactions without MISO.
ESP32 gpio_caps.h:11 says GPIO matrix delay25ns; soc.h:156 says APB80MHz; spi_flash_ll.h:30 says flash source80MHz; saved sdkconfig.h selects FLASHFREQ_80M.

Source-only arithmetic under that selected path gives divider1 and floor((1+0+25)*80000/1000000)=2, hence extra_dummy2. Actual trace merely shows one whole SSI byte consumed and cannot distinguish1 from2 subbyte clocks.

For QIO28/(5+2), combined56bits is already seven whole bytes; the new floor preserves that extra byte. Therefore resolving JEDEC0k does not by itself establish the later QIO transport. This is an explicit remaining runtime question, not a request to change firmware/config.
